interp_p27_band_reading.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, Fig. 9 n2-n3

interp_p27_n4_dose_bound.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, Fig. 9 n4
interp_p27_n4_dose_bound.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. A first prescription is ordered only for a dose within the printed start amount of that n4 line: amlodipine 5-10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5-25 mg and indapamide SR 1.5-2.5 mg (the printed range; no separate maximum is printed), and exactly enalapril 5 mg or lisinopril 2.5 mg (the one printed start dose; no other first amount is printed). A first dose above the printed start dose and at most the printed Max (enalapril 20 mg, lisinopril 40 mg) goes to clinical review (gap_p27_n4_start_dose). A dose of 0 mg or less, below the lowest printed start amount, or above the highest printed amount, is not a printed dose: it is kept as a refused choice, and the clinician is asked again. A lower first dose (for example for an older patient) therefore has no ordering path; the clinician may choose no n4 medicine. For captopril, losartan and nifedipine SR every positive dose goes to clinical review (gap_p27_n4_maximum); their printed start amounts are recorded but not checked. The frequency is the printed od or bid. Independent review M1, M2 and M4.

interp_p27_n5_potassium.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, Fig. 9 n5
interp_p27_n5_potassium.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. For an ACE inhibitor the clinician names the potassium result relied on. K is read in mmol/L (no unit is printed). K at most 5.5 permits the order; an unknown K leaves the choice unresolved (format section 5). A CCB or diuretic does not read K. A cited K of 0 mmol/L or less is not a measurement: it is read as an unknown K, so the issue names choice.potassium, the clinician collects it and chooses again. The figure prints no lower K; whether a clinical lower limit applies is a question for Kebba (final review F1). A K result of another patient is an issue: the attributed choice is kept as refused, an evidence review is owned, and the clinician chooses again (final review F2). Review question Q2 (F7).

interp_p28_urgency_exit.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.28, printed p.18, Hypertensive Emergency Management, Definition; PDF p.24, printed p.14, §II.A.1
interp_p28_urgency_exit.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. At the health centre, a second diagnostic reading with SBP above 180 or DBP above 120 (the p.28 urgency values, either value) leaves the Fig. 9 band for clinical review before pregnancy, the n5 comorbidities or the band are read. End-organ damage is not assessed at this step, so urgency and emergency are not told apart. A reading at or above the p.24 values 180/110 that is not above 180/120 stays in the Fig. 9 dual band, which also stops for review. Independent review M7.

format_s5_unresolved.note: Unknown information may be ignored only when it cannot change the selected outcome; otherwise unresolved and the information-resolution handler is invoked.

format_s5_unmatched_ambiguous.note: Unmatched invokes the unhandled-case handler; ambiguous records the conflict and invokes the review handler.

format_s6_handlers.note: A default is a named ordinary handler table; it cannot fabricate a clinical outcome; missing responsibility or an unresolved waiting limit is visible.

format_s8_preflight.note: Preflight the whole transition; structural errors and invalid bounds go to the failure handler without committing the parent transition.

format_s9_not_authorized.note: An unauthorized completion is retained as an attributed report and follows the not_authorized handler; it cannot make the decision.

format_s12_stop_and_preserve.note: The default stop_and_preserve policy cancels pending execution work, requests cancellation of dispatched work and retains history; independent work keeps its owner.

format_s12_unmet_work.note: Every delayed task has identity, link, owner, completion evidence and effective unmet-work behavior; a captured versioned policy binds shared tables to the work's events.

format_s7_immediate_steps.note: An emitted decision.requested is delivered after the initiating transition commits; the requested table evaluates in its own transition and trace.

interp_p12_maximum_intervals.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.12, printed p.2, Fig. 2 and N.B.; studio/decisions/conflict-rbcncd24-screening-interval.json
interp_p12_maximum_intervals.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. Reconciled with the accepted source reading: at least every five or three years sets a maximum interval, not a prohibition on earlier screening. From age 35 the annual note is shorter. A due date is the latest recall date, not a completed visit.

rbcncd24_p26_targets.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.26, printed p.16, adult hypertension
rbcncd24_p26_targets.note: Figure 8 gives office targets by age and condition. Ages 18–65: systolic 130 or lower if tolerated, not below 120, except the CKD cell. Ages 65–79 and 80 or older: systolic 130–139 if tolerated. All diastolic cells give 70–79. Age 65 overlaps. The CKD cell is not silently repaired.

interp_p26_target_check.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.26, printed p.16, adult hypertension
interp_p26_target_check.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. For the unambiguous non-CKD rows, a tolerated office reading is in target at 120–130/70–79 below age 65, and 130–139/70–79 above age 65. Out-of-range or not-tolerated readings require a clinician treatment decision, never an automatic dose change. The reference leaves exactly 65 and CKD at source gaps.

gap_p26_target_65_ckd.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.26, printed p.16, adult hypertension
gap_p26_target_65_ckd.note: Source ambiguity: the age-65 overlap and CKD cell have active records conflict-rbcncd24-target-at-65 and correction-rbcncd24-fig8-ckd-target in studio/decisions. No clinical resolution is recorded there. The reference does not choose a target for these cases.

interp_p25_followup_review.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.25, printed p.15, adult hypertension
interp_p25_followup_review.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. A named assessing clinician reviews the office reading, symptoms, organ damage, comorbidities, medicines, adherence, adverse effects, tolerance, renal safety and contraindications. A correlated host assessment attests these findings. This is a draft collection and accountability choice; the national text does not define the electronic form or its completion proof.

gap_p27_renewal_supply.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, adult hypertension
gap_p27_renewal_supply.note: Source silence in the hypertension chapter: no prescription validity, renewal authorization, dispensing, patient-receipt or controlled-patient review interval is stated. The reference records this limit after a supported decision. It does not equate a prescription with medicine supply.

gap_p27_longitudinal_excluded.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, adult hypertension
gap_p27_longitudinal_excluded.note: Scope exclusion and incomplete extraction: pregnancy, advanced CKD, specialist indications, hospital combinations, and urgent-care treatment have source text elsewhere (PDF pp.28–29,53,72–73). Their specialist treatment is not encoded here. This is not source silence. The facility SOP must name a receiving service and require handover acceptance.

gap_p27_regimen_change.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, adult hypertension
gap_p27_regimen_change.note: Incomplete extraction, not absence of national treatment: Figure 9 n12 permits up-titration and its later rows give combination regimens, but the full follow-up change/switch process is not encoded in this reference. In particular, a medicine change is not evidence that the patient already takes the new medicine at a dose above its printed starting amount. The facility must distinguish a new or restarted medicine from titration of the same active prescription, with an explicit proposed SOP.

rbcncd24_p53_diabetes_htn.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.53, printed p.43, Recommendations for BP control in diabetes
rbcncd24_p53_diabetes_htn.note: The condition-specific chapter recommends ACE inhibitor or ARB treatment for hypertension in diabetes and gives its own BP control recommendations. These constraints are not replaced by the uncomplicated Figure 9 preference readings.

rbcncd24_p73_ckd_htn.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.73, printed p.63, Figure 31
rbcncd24_p73_ckd_htn.note: The CKD hypertension algorithm starts ACE inhibitor or ARB treatment with or without CCB, and includes kidney-related restrictions and later steps. These are condition-specific constraints, not a free choice among the general monotherapy list.

gap_p53_p73_comorbid_regimen.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.53, printed p.43, diabetes BP control; PDF p.73, printed p.63, CKD Figure 31
gap_p53_p73_comorbid_regimen.note: Extraction/integration boundary: the applicable diabetes and CKD regimen constraints and exceptions are not fully encoded or independently reviewed in this module. The national source is not silent. Do not authorize an unrestricted general regimen here.

rbcncd24_p28_pregnancy.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.28, printed p.18, Recommendations for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy
rbcncd24_p28_pregnancy.note: Pregnancy has its own assessment and treatment recommendations at systolic >=140 and/or diastolic >=90 and a separate printed >=160/110 prompt-treatment/admission provision. This module excludes pregnancy before routine adult confirmation; it does not settle the severe slash notation or choose a pregnancy regimen.

gap_p12_annual_transition_anchor.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.12, printed p.2, Fig. 2 and annual-screening note
gap_p12_annual_transition_anchor.note: The annual requirement from age 35 also constrains recalls created before 35. The figure does not specify the first eligible appointment anchor. A five-year recall at ages 31-34, or a three-year recall at ages 33-34, could skip the first annual period. The reference records this scheduling detail instead of extending a recall beyond it. This is not a renewed conflict between the annual note and maximum intervals.

unknown_input_care.title: Preserve care with unassessed hypertension danger
unknown_input_care.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Assess the unassessed hypertension symptoms and organ-damage signs now. If prompt assessment is unavailable, arrange assessment or referral at least as urgent as the most urgent applicable national danger route. Preserve known urgent care and the current safe treatment. Keep missing signs unknown. Do not infer hypertension emergency, change a medicine from an unconfirmed diagnosis, or delay transfer for information.
